This is the master build brief for creating ReportCraft AI. Give this complete document to your AI coding assistant, development team, or website-building agent as the single source of product requirements. Build the application in phases, keep this specification as the acceptance baseline, and do not silently remove a requirement.

Product definition: ReportCraft AI is a cross-sector web application, with a desktop companion, that turns imported HTML pages/files, Excel workbooks, CSV datasets, and Word documents into structured, evidence-linked, professionally designed, fully editable PowerPoint reports. It combines deterministic data processing with AI-assisted interpretation and slide planning. AI must never invent figures or replace source data.

1. Product vision and outcomes
Help users create decision-ready reports without manually copying tables, charts, and narrative into slides.
Accept multiple source files in one project and preserve the relationship between every generated result and its source.
Extract text, tables, numeric data, dates, labels, images, and document structure from supported input formats.
Clean, validate, map, summarize, and analyze data before asking AI to interpret it.
Generate a slide outline and a complete presentation with charts, tables, key findings, risks, recommendations, and source notes.
Provide a full slide editor so users can change text, shapes, charts, tables, images, layout, theme, and ordering.
Export editable PowerPoint and shareable PDF, and allow users to save, duplicate, revise, and version projects.

3.1 Import experience
Drag-and-drop upload plus a browse-files control; accept multiple files in one project.
Validate file extension, MIME type, file size, and content signature; reject mismatches and unsafe files.
Display file name, type, size, upload state, extraction state, and any warnings.
Show a source preview before analysis: workbook sheets, CSV rows, Word sections/tables, or HTML structure.

4. Main end-to-end workflow
Create workspace and project; select report type, audience, language, reporting period, and desired slide count.
Upload HTML, Excel, CSV, and/or Word files. The project may include more than one source.
Inspect extraction previews and choose relevant sheets, tables, sections, and date ranges.
Clean and validate data: detect missing values, duplicates, inconsistent units, invalid dates, and outliers.
Map columns and source values to report concepts such as indicator, target, actual, period, location, unit, and disaggregation.
Run deterministic calculations and create charts/tables with traceable inputs.
Ask AI to summarize verified evidence, identify trends and gaps, draft findings, and propose recommendations.
Generate a slide outline. User can reorder, add, remove, or rewrite slides before generation.
Generate the deck using the selected theme and layout system.
Open the full slide editor, review content and sources, and make manual changes.
Export editable PPTX and optionally PDF; save the project and version.

6. AI behavior and evidence rules
AI is an assistant for interpretation and writing, not the calculation authority. Compute numeric results in tested code.
Every numeric statement, chart, and table must be traceable to a source file, sheet/table/section, row or page range, and calculation definition where applicable.
Never fabricate missing values, targets, dates, denominators, sources, or causal explanations. Clearly label assumptions and unknowns.
Separate observed facts, calculated results, AI interpretations, and recommendations in the internal data model and in user-facing review.
When sources conflict, show the conflict and ask the user to select or resolve the authoritative value.
Use retrieval-augmented prompting from extracted project content; send only the minimum necessary content to external AI providers.
Provide a configurable AI gateway: local models through Ollama and external API providers through provider adapters. Keep provider credentials server-side.
Allow AI model selection by administrator and, where enabled, by user. Show model/provider used and whether local or external processing occurred.
Support English and Afaan Oromoo output. Preserve original source language and allow translation/editing without changing numeric values.
Offer regeneration for selected text or slides, not only the entire deck. Retain user edits and provide undo/version history.

8. UX, visual design, and accessibility
Visual direction: modern, professional, calm, data-focused. Use deep navy/blue as the primary color with restrained gold accents and neutral backgrounds.
Keep layouts clean and compact; prioritize readable charts, clear hierarchy, whitespace, and consistent alignment.
Use a persistent left navigation for Dashboard, Projects, Templates, Sources, and Settings; show project workflow steps in context.
Use clear status labels: Draft, Uploading, Extracting, Needs review, Analyzing, Generating, Ready, Failed.
Provide empty states, progress indicators, inline validation, actionable errors, confirmation for destructive actions, and autosave status.
Use accessible contrast, keyboard navigation, meaningful labels, alt text, and screen-reader-friendly controls.
Build localization from the beginning: no hard-coded UI strings; support English and Afaan Oromoo text expansion and date/number formats.

11. Security, privacy, and reliability
Enforce authentication, workspace isolation, role-based authorization, and object-level permission checks on every API.
Validate uploads by size, extension, MIME type, and file signature; scan files where practical; store uploads outside the web root.
Protect HTML/URL import against server-side request forgery, local-network access, unsafe redirects, and malicious embedded content.
Sanitize rendered HTML; do not execute imported scripts, macros, or embedded active content.
Encrypt traffic with HTTPS; protect secrets and AI API keys using environment/secret management; never expose keys in the browser.
Use signed, time-limited download links; apply retention/deletion policies; provide project and source deletion.
Record audit events for login, sharing, export, deletion, role changes, and AI-provider usage.
Back up PostgreSQL and file storage; test restore procedures; monitor failed jobs, storage, API errors, and queue depth.
Provide clear disclosure when content is sent to an external AI provider; offer local-model mode where configured.

16. Build instructions for the AI coding agent or development team
Read this specification fully before generating code. Treat it as the product requirements baseline.
Start by proposing a concise implementation plan and repository structure, then implement Phase 0 and Phase 1.
Do not create a decorative prototype that cannot upload, parse, validate, analyze, and export real files.
Use real persistence and background jobs for long-running work; do not store user projects only in browser memory.
Create migrations, seed data, sample files, automated tests, and setup instructions with every relevant feature.
Keep the frontend and backend types/contracts documented. Validate all API inputs and outputs.
Implement one end-to-end vertical slice at a time and keep it runnable before moving to the next phase.
Use synthetic/demo data for examples. Never include real confidential reports or credentials in source control.
When a requirement cannot be implemented exactly, document the limitation and a safe alternative instead of silently omitting it.
At the end of each phase, report completed features, test results, known limitations, changed files, and exact run/deploy commands.
17. Initial release scope and exclusions

Must-have first release: authentication; project dashboard; HTML/XLSX/CSV/DOCX import; source preview; data cleaning and mapping; deterministic analytics; AI-assisted bilingual report outline and narrative; professional themes; editable PPTX generation; basic full slide editing; PDF export; project save/versioning.

Later enhancements: PDF/OCR import, PPTX import, collaboration and comments, public share links, advanced master-slide editing, Power BI connectivity, scheduled report generation, custom organization templates, and advanced desktop offline workflows.
Do not promise perfect extraction of every complex layout, formula, embedded object, or legacy file. Unsupported content must be reported clearly and safely.

19. Engineering decisions and non-negotiable implementation rules

This section converts the product brief into implementation constraints intended to reduce defects, rework, data loss, and unsafe behavior. Where an implementation choice differs, document the reason, trade-off, migration path, and acceptance impact before coding.
Decision area
Required rule
Reason / failure prevented
Architecture
Start as a modular monolith with explicit Django app boundaries; do not split into microservices in the first release.
Avoids distributed-system complexity and inconsistent transactions.
API contract
Use versioned REST APIs, OpenAPI schema generation, typed frontend API clients, and shared error conventions.
Prevents frontend/backend contract drift.
Data integrity
Use database constraints, transactions, idempotency keys for job submission, and immutable source versions.
Prevents duplicate jobs, partial writes, and overwritten evidence.
Long tasks
Run parsing, AI, analytics, and exports in Celery workers; return job IDs and status endpoints.
Prevents request timeouts and blocked web workers.
Slide document
Use one versioned, validated JSON slide-document schema as the editor's canonical state.
Prevents editor/export mismatch.
PPTX output
Generate editable PowerPoint objects from the canonical slide schema; do not flatten complete slides to images.
Preserves editability and downstream revision.
AI safety
AI output is a proposal; numeric calculations and source references are resolved by deterministic application code.
Prevents hallucinated values and false citations.
File safety
Treat all imported files and extracted HTML as untrusted input.
Prevents malicious content execution and parser abuse.
Migrations
Every schema change must have a Django migration and a tested rollback/forward plan.
Prevents environment drift and deployment failures.
Configuration
No secrets or environment-specific URLs in source code; validate required settings at startup.
Prevents credential leakage and fragile deployments.
20. Canonical data pipeline and provenance contract
All import adapters must produce a common extraction envelope. The raw source remains immutable; transformations create new derived artifacts with lineage back to the source.
20.1 Extraction envelope
Field
Purpose / validation
source_id
Stable database identifier for the uploaded source.
source_version
Immutable version number and SHA-256 checksum.
parser_name / parser_version
Identifies the exact parser used for reproducibility.
item_id
Stable identifier for an extracted item within a source version.
item_type
One of paragraph, heading, table, table_cell, image, worksheet, row, chart, metadata, or other enumerated type.
location_ref
Machine-readable source location: page, sheet, cell/range, table index, section path, row index, or DOM path.
content_payload
Typed content; do not coerce all values into strings.
warnings
Structured warnings with code, severity, message, and location.
created_at
UTC timestamp; display in user's configured timezone.
20.2 Lineage rules
Every derived dataset, metric, chart, table, AI finding, and slide element must carry one or more source-lineage references.
A lineage reference must identify source version and source location, not merely the uploaded filename.
When a source is replaced, create a new source version; never silently mutate the source used by an existing published export.
Store transformation definitions and versions so a calculation can be reproduced.
If a chart aggregates multiple rows, preserve the filter, grouping, aggregation function, and contributing source references.
If evidence cannot be traced, label it as user-entered or unverified and do not present it as source-derived.
21. Detailed validation, error handling and recovery
Every failure must be visible, actionable, logged with a correlation ID, and recoverable where possible. Do not expose stack traces, database details, secrets, or raw provider errors to end users.
Scenario
Expected application behavior
Recovery / acceptance test
Unsupported extension or MIME mismatch
Reject before processing; show accepted formats and actual detected type.
User can select a supported file; no source record remains in a failed half-state.
File exceeds configured limit
Reject with the configured size limit and guidance to split/compress.
Limit is enforced by proxy, API, and storage policy.
Corrupt or password-protected file
Mark extraction failed or needs input; preserve original upload if safe.
User can replace file or retry after removing password.
Excel has no header / merged cells
Show preview and ask user to choose header row or range; warn on ambiguous merged cells.
Selected mapping is persisted and re-runnable.
CSV delimiter / encoding unclear
Offer detected candidates and manual override; preview before commit.
Test comma, semicolon, tab, UTF-8, BOM, and malformed rows.
DOCX/HTML contains complex layout
Extract supported structures and report skipped elements with location.
No silent omission; user can inspect extraction warnings.
Parser crashes or times out
Worker marks job failed with safe error code; retry only if error is transient.
Retry is bounded and idempotent.
AI provider unavailable / rate limited
Queue with bounded exponential backoff; allow switch to local/alternate provider if configured.
No duplicate deck or loss of user edits.
AI returns malformed JSON
Validate against strict schema; retry with repair prompt once or twice, then fail safely.
Invalid response never reaches renderer.
PowerPoint export fails
Retain slide document; show export job error and allow retry.
User edits are not lost.
Browser closes during processing
Job continues server-side; dashboard restores status on return.
No dependency on browser tab remaining open.
Network disconnect during upload
Use resumable/chunked upload for large files where supported; verify checksum after completion.
Incomplete upload cannot enter analysis pipeline.
Concurrent edits
Use optimistic concurrency/version numbers; prompt on stale update.
Last-write-wins is not allowed for slide document edits.
Storage/database temporarily unavailable
Return service-unavailable response; retry safe operations; alert operators.
No partial success response.
User deletes project during active job
Cancel or safely detach jobs; prevent late job from recreating deleted records.
Deletion policy and worker race condition tested.
21.1 Standard API error shape
Use a stable JSON error envelope for all API errors. Example contract (illustrative):
"error": {
"code": "SOURCE_VALIDATION_FAILED",
"message": "The uploaded file could not be processed.",
"details": [{"field": "file", "reason": "Unsupported format"}],
"correlation_id": "server-generated-id",
"retryable": false

Use appropriate HTTP status codes: 400 invalid request, 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 not found, 409 version conflict, 413 payload too large, 415 unsupported media type, 422 semantic validation failure, 429 rate limit, and 500/503 unexpected or temporary service failure.

23. AI orchestration contract
The AI gateway must isolate provider-specific APIs from business logic. Prompts, output schemas, provider settings, token budgets, and model identifiers must be versioned.

Risk
Mitigation

Single canonical slide schema; explicit export support matrix; visual regression and cross-office testing.

Deterministic calculation engine; evidence IDs; numeric consistency checks; user approval.

Local model option, explicit provider disclosure, minimal evidence transfer, configurable policy.

Quotas, job limits, storage lifecycle, local deployment option, and usage visibility.
30. Final master instruction — copy this into the coding agent

You are the lead product engineer for ReportCraft AI. Build the production-oriented application described in this specification. Before coding, inspect the repository and report its current state. Then produce an implementation plan mapped to the numbered phases and acceptance criteria. Do not replace required working functionality with mock buttons or static screens. Implement the smallest complete vertical slice first: authenticate → create project → upload HTML/XLSX/CSV/DOCX → inspect extraction preview → map data → calculate verified metrics → create evidence-grounded report outline → generate editable PPTX → edit a slide → export PPTX/PDF. Use React + TypeScript, Django REST Framework, PostgreSQL, Celery/Redis, private object storage, and a versioned canonical slide JSON schema unless an explicit architecture decision justifies an alternative. Treat imported files as untrusted. Keep source files immutable and preserve provenance. AI may draft language and propose visuals, but deterministic code owns calculations. Validate every AI response and every slide document. Add migrations, automated tests, error handling, logging, security controls, and setup/deployment documentation as part of each phase. Never claim a feature is complete until its acceptance tests pass. At the end of each development iteration, report: completed requirements, changed files, commands to run, tests and results, known limitations, risks, and next phase.
Appendix B. Practical first sprint
Create monorepo and Docker Compose services; add health checks and environment validation.
Create Django project, accounts, workspace, project, and source models with migrations.
Build React shell, login, project dashboard, create-project flow, and API client.
Implement private upload endpoint with file size/type validation, checksum, and immutable source record.
Implement one parser adapter each for CSV, XLSX, DOCX, and HTML with fixture-based tests.
Add asynchronous extraction task and source preview API; display parser warnings in the UI.
Demonstrate upload-to-preview for all four formats before starting AI features.
Appendix C. Important scope clarifications
CSV is the correct extension (not CVS). The interface may display 'CSV spreadsheet' to users.
HTML upload means processing an uploaded HTML file in the first release. Importing arbitrary public URLs is a separate feature requiring additional SSRF and network-safety controls.
DOCX and XLSX are the recommended modern Word and Excel formats. Legacy DOC and XLS should be explicitly tested or routed through a documented conversion step.
PPTX editability is feature-dependent. Native text, shapes, tables, and common charts are the baseline; advanced effects and uncommon chart features need a support matrix.
A desktop build using Tauri 2 is a packaging and local-integration phase, not a prerequisite for the first web release.
